title: Number bonds & fact families
examples: Can you show me a fact family for the number five?
What do you mean by inverse facts?
How do I use a fact triangle?

explain.say: A number bond shows two parts that make a whole. Look at these five counters.
Split the five counters into two and three. Two and three are the parts. Five is the whole.
You can split five in other ways too. Four and one also make five.
A fact family uses the same three numbers. Three, four and seven make one fact family.
Three plus four is seven. Four plus three is seven. Seven take away three is four. Seven take away four is three.
When you know one fact, you know all four. The whole is the biggest number.

faq.a: A number bond shows two parts that join to make a whole. For example, two and three make five.
asks: How do I see the parts and the whole?

faq.a: Inverse facts are the opposite facts. If you know that two plus three equals five, then you also know that five minus two equals three.

faq.q: How do I use a fact triangle?
faq.a: In a fact triangle, the largest number at the top is the whole. The two numbers at the bottom are the parts that make it.
asks: Is the top number always the biggest?

faq.q: Can I use number bonds for bigger numbers?
faq.a: Yes, you can use them for numbers up to twenty or even up to one hundred. The idea stays the same.

faq.q: What if I forget one part?
faq.a: Use the fact family or the triangle to help. Take the part you know away from the whole.
asks: What if I need to find a missing number?

facts: A number bond shows parts joining to make a whole.
Fact families use addition and subtraction together.
In a fact triangle, the top number is always the whole.
If two numbers make a total, they are a number bond pair.

quiz.say: Look at the counters. Tap the sum that matches.
quiz.why: There are 2 red and 3 blue counters. Together they make 5.

wrong.0: This sum misses one blue counter, because there are 3 blue ones.
wrong.1: This sum has one red counter too many, because there are 2 red ones.

quiz.say: Join the two parts. Tap the whole.
quiz.why: Count on 4 from 6: 7, 8, 9, 10. The whole is 10.

wrong.0: The number 2 is 6 take away 4, but the parts join to make the whole.

quiz.say: Find the missing part. Tap it.
quiz.why: 7 and 3 make 10. So the missing part is 3.

wrong.0: Count on from 7: 8, 9, 10 makes three more.
wrong.1: The number 17 is 10 and 7 added, but a part is smaller than the whole.
